facts.F14: Confirmed Ratchet design: the compiled IL decides every list entry. Each list is inline, measured from the IL during C1, keyed by full type name (nested types reduced to their top-level type), and compared both ways (a missing entry and an extra entry both fail). Where a short name is shared, the key is the full name (D-1 outcome record: the moved AzureDevOps WorkItemExtensions versus Lighthouse.Backend.Extensions.WorkItemExtensions). The Expected baseline column of the Ratchet design is a guess: an entry the design did not foresee is recorded in the list and reported to the host with the IL edge that forced it, never silently accepted; an expected entry the IL does not show is left out and reported the same way. Lists only shrink after C.

facts.F22: Layer algebra, test side only (production unchanged, D-0, D-10, D-12): state = the finite set of top-level type-to-type IL edges of the production assembly and the finite set of source and test file paths; operation = evaluate a rule over that state with an inline list; observation = a verdict naming each offender, each missing list entry and each extra list entry. Carriers: InboundVerdict, OutboundVerdict and KernelRuleVerdict owned by Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Architecture/ModuleRules.cs; the module wording is a ModuleWording value owned by the new boundaries file; membership facts are owned by TrackerIntegrationMembership. No per-process state.
facts.F23: Formal verification not applicable (feature-delta Formal verification section, Confirmed): every claim is an exact equality over finite sets read from the compiled IL and the file tree, decided exhaustively by the rule itself with a made-up offender per position as falsifier. There is no state transition, ordering, concurrency, recovery or liveness claim, so no Quint, TLA+/TLC or Agda model is selected; a model would restate the namespace map and could not fail. Liveness is not applicable: nothing runs over time. Treatment of each law is Finite; property-based testing is not applicable to a closed finite domain.
